newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu ends stable, market stagnant.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu ends stable, market stagnant.

text.p: Romania's leu closed static near 7,000 to the dollar on Tuesday on a quiet interbank market with operators saying the currency might stabilise in the next few days.
"It seems the leu enjoys being on the 7,000 level. Some traders tried to sell dollars at better rates but nobody rushed to strike deals at those prices," said one trader.
Most dealers said the money market remained liquid with short-term funds at 225 percent for overnight and one-week rates near 250 percent.

Some traders reacted to the central bank (BNR) announcement that it would release a once-a-week list of daily exchange rates for the leu to replace a former reference rate which was made public every day.

"Several banks in the market are planning to work out a rate at noon," said Paul Dinescu from the Bucharest subsidiary of Dutch bank ABN Amro. Dinescu declined to say how many banks would be involved and gave no details of the method to be used to set the rate.

On Tuesday, the BNR said it would compute a daily exchange rate for the leu as an average of prices on the local foreign exchange market but it said the method of computing that rate remained confidential.
Last month, the BNR gave up computing the leu's reference rate after restoring local dealer licences to 24 banks, which are now market makers along with four others.

It had postponed announcing a new method of computing the exchange rate for two consecutive weeks, after freezing the reference rate at its latest value of 7,744 lei to the dollar, computed on February 19. That rate is in force until Tuesday midnight.
Banks' quotes continued to show a wide range, with leu- dollar rates from 6,200/100 to 7,400/8,400.
Leu-dollar retail prices weakened slightly towards 7,100/400 from some 7,000/200 in early trading.
